new_scholarship.name: International Excellence Entrance Scholarship
new_scholarship.duration: Multi-year, exact renewal terms not published on the award page
new_scholarship.application_period: Application for the 2027/28 award is open at the time of verification. The complete application, all required documentation and the recommender's letter must be received by 1 December.
new_scholarship.application_method: Separate application via the University of Manitoba award application, in addition to the admission application
new_scholarship.description: The University of Manitoba International Excellence Entrance Scholarship is a competitive international award for high school graduates who combine academic giftedness with leadership and sustained community involvement. Three awards are made each year: one valued at $25,000 and two valued at $10,000 each. Applicants are ranked first, second and third from the award application together with the admissions application.
new_scholarship.best_fit: International high school graduates applying to a University 1 or direct-entry programme at the University of Manitoba, with a 90%+ admission average for the top award and a record of leadership and community involvement.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: International students applying to a University 1 or direct-entry programme. The $25,000 first-place award requires a 90% admission average across five specified senior courses; the two $10,000 awards require only the minimum admission requirements. All tiers require leadership and community involvement and a completed admission application by 1 December.
eligibility: Minimum admission average of 90% across five of the following senior level high school courses: Math, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Sciences, English, First Language Literature, Geography, History, Music, Visual Arts (required for the $25,000 award)
Achieved the minimum admission requirements for University 1 or any faculty, college or school with a direct entry option (route for the two $10,000 awards)
Enrolled full-time, minimum 80% course load, in the first year of study (stated for the $25,000 award)
Demonstrated strong leadership qualities and sustained, meaningful community involvement
Completed a University of Manitoba application for admission by 1 December, including payment of the application fee
Provided one letter of recommendation from a current teacher or principal, translated into English if required
coverage: Scholarship funding toward tuition for an undergraduate degree programme
Exact covered-expense breakdown is not published on the award page
benefits: Ranking into first, second and third place based on the award application and the admissions application
requirements: Submit the award application with all documentation by 1 December
Secure a recommender who can submit a letter by 1 December
Pay the University of Manitoba application fee with the admission application
required_documents: One letter of recommendation from a current teacher or principal, translated into English if required
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Short-listed applicants are ranked into first, second and third place using the results of the award application together with the admissions application. The recommender must be a current teacher or principal.
new_scholarship.notes: Only three awards are made per year, so this is a genuinely competitive award rather than an automatic entitlement. Renewal duration is not stated on the award page.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply for admission to a University 1 or direct-entry programme at the University of Manitoba and pay the application fee by 1 December
Submit the separate award application with all documentation by 1 December
Ask a current teacher or principal for a reference, and confirm they can submit before 1 December
Target a 90% average across five of the listed senior courses if you are applying for the $25,000 award
Plan to enrol full-time with a minimum 80% course load in first year if you are applying for the $25,000 award
Document leadership roles and sustained community involvement before applying
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 December deadline, which is absolute for every part of the application including the reference
Recommender cannot deliver the letter in time - the University notes this is a common failure point
Applying for the $25,000 award with an average below 90% across five listed courses
Using a reference who is not a current teacher or principal
Not paying the admission application fee with the application
Assuming the 90% average requirement applies to the $10,000 awards - it does not
estimated_uncovered_costs: Whatever the award does not cover, since the page publishes no covered-expense breakdown
Second and subsequent year funding is not guaranteed by anything published on the page
Travel, immigration and permanent residence costs
document_audit: One letter of recommendation from a current teacher or principal, translated into English if required
Admission application with the application fee paid by 1 December
No transcript checklist is published on the award page beyond the admission average requirement
